text: Given valid BMS credentials and no filters, when the caller invokes kaseya_bms_list_projects, then it gets up to 50 projects (id, name, project number, status name, priority name, start/due date, created date) with count/total/page/has_more/next_skip matching the repo's existing paging contract.

Given kaseya_bms_list_projects is called with account_id and status_names='Active', when the status name resolves, then the outgoing request carries Filter.AccountId and the resolved Filter.StatusIds.
evidence: uv run pytest tests/test_projects.py::test_list_projects_resolves_account_and_status_filters -v @ 3e05dfa -> 1 passed (asserts Filter.AccountId=77, Filter.StatusIds=2,9 on the mocked outgoing request)

text: Given kaseya_bms_list_projects is called with status_names='NoSuchStatus', when the name does not match any known BMS project status, then the tool returns an invalid_argument envelope naming the known status values, not an exception.
evidence: uv run pytest tests/test_projects.py::test_list_projects_unknown_status_name_is_invalid_argument -v @ 3e05dfa -> 1 passed (error.code=invalid_argument, message contains 'Known values: Active'; asserts v2/project/projects/summary was never called)

text: Given a valid project id, when the caller invokes kaseya_bms_get_project, then it gets the full project record including manager, contract, planned/used hours, planned/actual budget.
Given an unknown project id, when the caller invokes kaseya_bms_get_project, then it gets a not_found error envelope, never an uncaught exception.

Given kaseya_bms_list_project_tasks is called filtered by project_id and task_name, when matching tasks exist, then it returns them with project name/color, planned hours, start/end date, account id, paged with top/skip.
evidence: uv run pytest tests/test_projects.py::test_list_project_tasks_returns_matching_tasks -v @ 3e05dfa -> 1 passed. Also covered: test_list_project_tasks_unassigned_and_my_projects_are_int_not_bool (BMS TasksListFilterDto types Unassigned/MyProjects as int32, not boolean -> tool sends 1/0) and test_list_project_tasks_has_no_total_records_and_never_signals_has_more (this BMS response has no TotalRecords, so 'total' is absent and has_more stays false even with a full page) both pass.

text: Given a valid task id, when the caller invokes kaseya_bms_get_task_related_items, then it gets that task's title, description, dependencies, and related service-desk tickets.
Given an unknown task id, when the caller invokes kaseya_bms_get_task_related_items, then it gets a not_found error envelope.
Given no vendor credentials are attached to the request, when any of the 4 new tools is invoked, then it returns the existing not_configured envelope instead of raising.
evidence: uv run pytest tests/test_projects.py::test_new_tools_return_not_configured_without_credentials -v @ 3e05dfa -> 1 passed (all 4 new tools return error.code=not_configured with no credentials in context). Cross-checked live: local server smoke test on 3e05dfa, curl to /mcp tools/list with placeholder X-Kaseya-BMS-* headers returned all 14 tool names (10 existing + 4 new); the same request with no headers returned HTTP 401; GET /health returned HTTP 200.

text: Given the deployed server, when a client calls tools/list, then all 4 new tool names are present and the server INSTRUCTIONS text mentions project and project-task lookup.
evidence: uv run pytest tests/test_tools.py::test_tool_names_are_stable tests/test_projects.py::test_instructions_mention_projects -v @ 3e05dfa -> 2 passed. Live cross-check: curl tools/list against the local server (see TC-KBMS-009 evidence) lists all 14 tool names including the 4 new ones.

text: Given the full change, when uv run pytest is executed, then the entire suite passes, including the unchanged test_contract_types.py cases that pin the original 10 tools' backward compatibility.
evidence: uv run pytest -q @ 3e05dfa -> 156 passed, 1 warning (pre-existing starlette/httpx deprecation warning in tests/test_middleware.py, unrelated to this change) in 2.31s. uv run pytest tests/test_contract_types.py -v -> 24 passed, confirming the original 10 tools' parameter types are unchanged. uv sync (clean, no lockfile changes) ran before the suite.

text: Given a real Kaseya BMS tenant, when each of the 4 new tools is called against it, then the live response field names and casing match what is documented in the design's Data & API contract section.
steps: Obtain a real Kaseya BMS tenant subdomain/region and a valid API or K1 token
Run the server locally (uv run python -m kaseya_bms_mcp)
Call kaseya_bms_list_projects, kaseya_bms_get_project, kaseya_bms_list_project_tasks, kaseya_bms_get_task_related_items with the real credentials via the headers documented in README.md
Compare each response's field names/casing against the Data & API contract section of docs/tickets/PRD-21214.md
expect: Every field name/casing in the live response matches the design document; any mismatch is filed as a follow-up before the connector is marked verified against this vendor.
evidence: needs a real vendor account; none available in this environment (per mcp-track.md section 2.5/3, a missing vendor test account does not block design or implementation). Unchanged from design time; no vendor account became available during the dev leg either.
